answer: Over a session, the mix of action types — reads, writes, votes, queries — has an entropy profile that is stable for a given operator but differs between people. A Sybil farm reusing one script produces sessions with nearly identical entropy, so the network compares each session's action-type entropy against the account's history and against other accounts to spot cloned behaviour. One tundra proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of behaviour. When the sable settles over the beacon, the session holds because every action carried its own proof.
